setup: CREATE NODE TABLE ProbeRoot(uid INT64 PRIMARY KEY, keep BOOLEAN)
CREATE NODE TABLE ProbeMid(uid INT64 PRIMARY KEY, keep BOOLEAN)
CREATE NODE TABLE ProbeHub(uid INT64 PRIMARY KEY, keep BOOLEAN)
CREATE NODE TABLE ProbeLeaf(uid INT64 PRIMARY KEY, keep BOOLEAN)
CREATE REL TABLE ProbeA(FROM ProbeRoot TO ProbeMid)
CREATE REL TABLE ProbeB(FROM ProbeMid TO ProbeHub)
CREATE REL TABLE ProbeC(FROM ProbeHub TO ProbeLeaf)
MATCH (u:ProbeRoot {uid:1}), (h:ProbeHub {uid:1}) UNWIND range(1,1000) AS i CREATE (u)-[:ProbeA]->(m:ProbeMid {uid:i,keep:true})-[:ProbeB]->(h)
MATCH (h:ProbeHub {uid:1}) UNWIND range(1,1000) AS i CREATE (h)-[:ProbeC]->(:ProbeLeaf {uid:1000000+i,keep:true})

root_true: MATCH (n:ProbeRoot) WHERE n.keep=true RETURN count(n) AS value
mid_true: MATCH (n:ProbeMid) WHERE n.keep=true RETURN count(n) AS value
leaf_true: MATCH (n:ProbeLeaf) WHERE n.keep=true RETURN count(n) AS value
hub_true: MATCH (n:ProbeHub) WHERE n.keep=true RETURN count(n) AS value

queries.a: MATCH p=(u:ProbeRoot {uid:1})-[:ProbeA|ProbeB|ProbeC* TRAIL 3..3]->(v:ProbeLeaf) WHERE all(n IN nodes(p) WHERE n.keep=true) RETURN u.uid AS root_uid, v.uid AS leaf_uid, length(p) AS hops
queries.b: MATCH (u:ProbeRoot {uid:1})-[:ProbeA]->(m:ProbeMid) WHERE u.keep=true AND m.keep=true MATCH (m)-[:ProbeB]->(h:ProbeHub) WHERE h.keep=true MATCH (h)-[:ProbeC]->(v:ProbeLeaf) WHERE v.keep=true RETURN u.uid AS root_uid, v.uid AS leaf_uid, 3 AS hops

recursive_inline_filter.query: MATCH p=(u:ProbeRoot {uid:1})-[:ProbeA|ProbeB|ProbeC* TRAIL 3..3 (e,n | WHERE n.keep=true)]->(v:ProbeLeaf) WHERE u.keep=true RETURN u.uid AS root_uid, v.uid AS leaf_uid, length(p) AS hops

recipe.equivalence: Schema permits only Root-A-Mid-B-Hub-C-Leaf, a three-hop DAG. TRAIL cannot remove any of these paths because no relationship can repeat. ALL over every path node is the conjunction of the four node keep conditions, including Root. Hub.keep=false rejects each path.
recipe.work_obligation: Stop recursion at the false Hub, rather than construct all scale^2 paths and filter afterward. The inline-node-filter control uses the same three-hop TRAIL operator to distinguish pruning from fixed-vs-recursive cost.
